items.anchor_quote: improbable that a single-moment device can be sensitive across the smoke particle size spectrum
items.summary: Because spacecraft fire scenarios involve a wider array of materials and heating conditions than tested, and spacecraft background aerosols can be quite large, Meyer et al. judge it improbable that a single-moment detector can be sensitive across the smoke particle size range while also resisting false alarms. items.location: Appendix B, Detector Design Requirement Implications
items.anchor_quote: Consequently a specification for a single particle size (or no size specification) would be risky.
items.summary: Comparing detector technologies against one hypothetical alarm-requirement aerosol, the authors find that a single-moment detector may be too sensitive (for example to dust) or not sensitive enough depending on particle size, so a single-size (or no-size) alarm specification would be risky; they note this is essentially the case for the current ISS and STS detectors, which are tuned to different size ranges. They suggest alarm requirements with criteria spanning the expected fire particulate sizes (e.g. 200 to 1200 nm) and detectors combining two moment measurements, which might also help reduce false alarms.
items.scope_notes: Design-requirement reasoning based on calculated detector responses (Figs. 3-4), not on observed alarms.

items.anchor_quote: detection methods that can measure more than one moment of the size distribution may show
items.summary: SAME-2 conclusions: under SAME conditions all samples produced significant numbers of sub-micron particles that an ionization detector readily detects; aging suggests some materials (e.g. silicone rubber) produce smoke large enough to be better detected by light scattering; zero-flow particles were 2 to 3 times larger than at the nominal 8 cm/s; broad size distributions are expected from credible pre-fire overheat events. The authors suggest that detectors measuring more than one moment may show more successful detection and false-alarm rejection than single-moment detectors, and call the prototype 2-moment MPASS results very encouraging.
items.scope_notes: Hedged ('may show'); MPASS evaluated by correlation against the other SAME instruments, not in a false-alarm test. Meyer et al. 2018 conclusions instead give zero-flow particles as on average double the 8.1 cm/s size.
